entries.title: cleanFilesFastFVA(false) fails when there are log files to remove
entries.why: m is assigned only inside 'if userInteraction' (lines 35-37) but line 39 evaluates strcmpi(m,'y') first, so cleanFilesFastFVA(false) with log files present hits an undefined m; the documented false option fails.

entries.title: The hierarchical method returns the requested maximum k as the number of clusters
entries.why: Line 173 sets k = kMax after the pre-order labelling; with n=4 < kMax=20 the cutoff is -Inf (line 117) and 4 clusters are labelled, yet k and eco.k (line 185) are 20, contradicting OUTPUTS 'k: number of clusters' (dbscan branch uses numel(unique), line 179).

entries.title: The status variable is named status_c<id>, not status as documented
entries.why: Line 67 names the variable sprintf('status_c%d', clusterId) while OUTPUT (lines 19-21) documents a variable `status`; by the rule's literal reading the documented result is not produced. Borderline: the code is deliberate and only the name differs, so the campaign could equally call this cosmetic.

notes: One entry is a doc/code mismatch where the code looks deliberate; AGREE under the literal rule, but the campaign should apply this reading consistently.

entries.title: Zero band applied inconsistently to the maximum and to max - min
entries.why: Lines 75 (mx < delta) and 68/85 (abs(mx-mn) < delta) use strict inequalities while the documented table treats |x| <= delta as zero; delta = 0 is accepted (line 57), and then -1, -3 and 3 can never be produced, e.g. [-1 2 -2],[0 2 -2],0 gives [5 2 -2]. Caveat: the second default-band example (2 vs 2+1e-9) is not a valid witness, because in double precision the difference is 1.00000008e-9 > 1e-9, so 2 is correct even with <=; the first element (-1 vs 1e-9 giving 5) and the delta=0 case stand.

notes: Fix the second default-band trigger: 2+1e-9 minus 2 is 1.00000008e-9 > 1e-9, so it does not show the defect. Use e.g. [2 2+5e-10] or the delta = 0 case.

entries.title: clusters without points are matched to a reference cluster instead of NaN, and an empty reference cluster absorbs unmatched clusters
entries.why: Line 63: with an all-NaN column, valid is empty and all([]) is true, so a cluster without points gets the first reference label (first trigger: clusterMap(4)=1), contradicting OUTPUT 'clusterMap ... (NaN for clusters without points)' (line 27); the self-match case relabels cluster 3 to the empty reference cluster 2.

entries.title: Every call stops at the undefined variable addGrRulesLinked
entries.why: addGrRulesLinked is never assigned in this function (used at lines 57 and 72), so every call stops at line 57.

entries.title: The hyperlink format string is read from the undefined variable command
entries.why: Lines 92, 95, 98 and 100 use the unassigned variable command; hyperlinkCommand (lines 39-41) is used only at line 73, so these lines would fail once line 57 is fixed.

entries.title: A model without rules and without grRules stops at a reference to the missing field rules
entries.why: The elseif at line 47 explicitly handles a model without rules and grRules but sizes the new field with numel(model.rules), the missing field, so the handling branch itself errors.

entries.title: Resources of an earlier controlled-vocabulary term leak into a later term with fewer identifiers
entries.why: Line 170 assigns to cRessourcestruct (lower-case s) while lines 171-174 fill cRessourceStruct, which keeps elements from the previous term, so a later term with fewer IDs keeps stale resources or deal fails on the size mismatch.

entries.title: A character vector for the ids option stops the call
entries.why: The ids validator (line 38) accepts char and the doc says 'A specific ID'; numElements = length(ids) (line 54) counts characters while relPos (line 57) selects one reaction, so the concatenation at line 92 fails (and ids{i} at line 138 would fail too).

entries.title: Errors when no reaction is selected
entries.why: When no row meets numModelsPresent, rxnsOfInterest is empty, max(max(...)) is empty and 'maxFluxUnits ~= 0 && ...' at line 68 throws a non-scalar && error; a valid threshold that selects nothing should give an empty result.

entries.title: The output is a cell array of reaction identifiers, not a table of fluxes
entries.why: Line 52 returns table2cell of the rxn column (a cell of IDs), whereas OUTPUT documents a table of fluxes per reaction and model. Under the rule's literal reading this is wrong-result; as the entry notes, the code is deliberate and the header is the likely error, so cosmetic is defensible. The function is quarantined by the first entry in any case.

notes: One entry is a doc/code mismatch where the code looks deliberate; AGREE under the literal rule, but the campaign should apply this reading consistently.

entries.title: The documented output is not assigned with the default printLevel, so a call requesting it stops
entries.why: With a C field and printLevel 0 (the default, line 25), the report is built only inside 'if printLevel > 0' (line 34) and the else at line 87 covers only a model without C, so a call that requests coupledRxnReport gets an unassigned-output error.

entries.title: The documented calls without rxnNameFlag stop with an error
entries.why: rxnNameFlag is documented as optional but has no default; line 36 'if rxnNameFlag' raises 'Not enough input arguments' for the documented usage printFluxBounds(model, rxns).

entries.title: The fixed-point format is never used together with reaction names
entries.why: Line 37's '& 0' deliberately disables the fixed-point branch; the header documents no print format, so the exponential output contradicts no documentation or result. At most a style or cleanup note, and it does not quarantine either way.

entries.title: The last sample of the file is not written to the subset file
entries.why: Line 61 loops j = 1:length(keep)-1, so the last entry of keep (the last sample read) is never written, contradicting OUTPUT 'containing only the requested subset' for every sample.

entries.title: The subset file is left open
entries.why: There is no fclose for the fid opened at line 60, so the handle leaks. No rule category fits exactly (it is not an undocumented input), but non-quarantining is right.

entries.title: A row cell array rxn_set together with KO stops with an error
entries.why: rxn_set is validated only by iscell (line 95) and documented as a 'Cell array'; line 139 does [rxn_set; {KO}], which fails for a 1xN row cell. The documented input fails when combined with KO.

entries.title: The enumeration writes tmp.mat into the current folder
entries.why: Lines 305 and 521 save tmp.mat in pwd and never remove it. This is an undocumented side effect, non-quarantining.

entries.title: The local threshold is the sum divided by the row length minus one, not the mean
entries.why: Line 60: avg = expressionSum/length(row)-1 is (sum/len)-1 by precedence, and row includes the gene ID column, so it is neither the mean nor sum/(len-1): (10+20)/3-1 = 9 instead of 15, which lets g1 pass the local test.

entries.title: Errors when no gene qualifies
entries.why: genes is assigned only inside the loop (lines 62-65); when no gene qualifies it is unassigned and the function errors on return (outside the try), whereas an empty list is the natural result for a valid threshold.

entries.title: The local threshold is the sum divided by the row length minus one, not the mean
entries.why: Same precedence bug (line 66 in this file): avg = 30/3-1 = 9 < 10, so g1 is not reported Local although its mean over the two sheets is 15 > 10.

entries.title: Errors when no gene qualifies
entries.why: With threshold -100 no gene is below the global threshold, and with avg 9 and 0.33 none is below the local one, so genes is never assigned and the function errors on return.

entries.title: The local threshold is the sum divided by the row length minus one, not the mean
entries.why: Line 67 has the same precedence bug: avg = 9 <= 10, so g1 (10, between lower 5 and upper 100) is reported High/Local although its mean 15 > 10.

entries.title: Errors when no gene qualifies
entries.why: With (100, 200) neither branch (lines 55, 61) fires for g1=10 or g2=2, so genes is never assigned and the function errors on return.

entries.title: The local threshold is the sum divided by the row length minus one, not the mean
entries.why: Line 67 has the same precedence bug: avg = 9 is not > 10, so g1 is not reported Low/Local although its mean 15 > 10.

entries.title: Errors when no gene qualifies
entries.why: With (-100, -50) no branch fires, so genes is unassigned and the function errors on return.

entries.title: Genes are matched by row position, not by gene ID
entries.why: Lines 30-32 take trTarget.Data(i) by row position, not by Geneid; the header requires no common order, so a reordered target silently pairs a gene with another gene's value, contradicting OUTPUT 'geneId, source ... value, target dataset expression value'. Somewhat borderline (an unstated same-order assumption), but the rule gives wrong-result for an input the doc does not exclude.

entries.title: Errors when the source sheet holds no gene
entries.why: With an empty source sheet the loop at line 29 never runs and result is unassigned (error on return, outside the try). Limitation is reasonable for a degenerate input.

entries.title: 'initialize' reads modelCom.indCom before building it from infoCom
entries.why: Lines 72-73 read modelCom.indCom before the check at line 76 that would build it from infoCom (line 82); the documented 'at least one of infoCom/indCom' input with only infoCom fails.

entries.title: Every call stops with an error when the taxonomy is prepared for export
entries.why: Line 260 sets taxonCol = 'Phylum' (char) and line 262 uses taxonCol+1:end as a column range; the clear intent is a column index (as at line 266), and on R2025a this raises the colon-operand error for every call that gets this far.

entries.title: Features with negative values are dropped as if they were all zero
entries.why: Line 63 drops rows with sum < 1e-4 under the comment 'remove fluxes that are all zeros' (line 58), so features with negative values (or values that cancel) are removed and not plotted; lines 188-189 likewise overwrite a group whose values sum to zero. This contradicts the code's evident intent.

entries.title: Box plots print the handle array of every plot
entries.why: cobraBoxplot returns h (src/base/utilities/toolboxFree/cobraBoxplot.m line 1); lines 102 and 199 have no semicolon, so the handle array is echoed. Cosmetic.

entries.title: Samples whose values are all zero are not removed
entries.why: Line 75 applies str2double to the data cells, which gives NaN for numeric cells (numeric cells are what line 124's cell2mat requires on R202x), so abs(sum(NaN)) < 1e-7 is never true and all-zero samples are not removed, contrary to the comment at line 71.

entries.title: Fecal exchange features never get a metabolite description
entries.why: Line 230 tests ~any(~contains(Statistics(:,1),'[fe]')) over a column that includes the header 'Feature' (line 92/95), so it is always false and the EX_/[fe] stripping (lines 231-232) never runs; [fe] features get 'NA' descriptions. This is code that is never reached.

entries.title: The documented orientation of the flux table and relative file paths stop with an error
entries.why: fluxPath is documented with samples as rows (lines 16-18), but line 37 compares the first row of fluxes (the reaction IDs in that layout) with the sample IDs and errors, with no transposition. Line 26 cd's into Metabolite_plots before reading, so relative paths fail.

entries.title: The current folder stays Metabolite_plots after an error
entries.why: After the error at line 38 the cd .. at line 90 is not reached, so the caller is left in Metabolite_plots. A side effect; non-quarantining is right.

entries.title: Errors when the first sample is infeasible and a later one is feasible
entries.why: valNames gets the 'Rxn' header only when k == 1 (line 70); if sample 1 was skipped as infeasible (lines 59-60, intended behaviour), the first feasible sample gets 4 header columns against 5 data columns and line 76 fails to concatenate.

entries.title: Uptake of an exchange missing from a sample is copied from the previous sample
entries.why: sp is reset per sample at line 81, but up never is; when x is empty (e == 1) line 96 is skipped and up(i) keeps the previous sample's value, so the uptake of a missing exchange is copied, unlike the secretion.

entries.title: The feasibility of every diet is read from the last diet
entries.why: Line 72 tests netProduction{fl,k} (the last diet) instead of netProduction{j,k}, so a diet's feasibility is taken from another diet: rich-diet results become NaN when the input diet is infeasible.

entries.title: Two samples stop with an error in the PCoA
entries.why: With 2 samples cobraPdist returns a scalar, and cobraCmdscale treats a scalar as a 1x1 matrix and rejects a nonzero diagonal. sampNames has no documented minimum, and the 'too few individuals' guard (line 124) comes after the failing call at lines 119-120.

entries.title: A structure without a rxns field is silently not saved
entries.why: Line 15 'if isfield(data,'rxns')' has no else branch, so any struct without rxns is silently not saved, contradicting the header 'Saves a data variable'.

entries.title: The heatmap shows only the first four individuals
entries.why: Line 48 hard-codes reacPat(:,2:5), so only 4 individuals are shown although line 52 sets one tick per individual (length(patOrg)). It would also fail with fewer than 4 individuals.

entries.title: The documented matrix inputs stop with an error
entries.why: reacPat and reacTab are documented as a matrix and a binary matrix (lines 15-18), but lines 48, 101 and 169 call table2cell on them, so plain matrices fail. Literally error, although the real caller passes tables and the header type is the likely mistake.

notes: One entry is a doc/code mismatch where the code looks deliberate; AGREE under the literal rule, but the campaign should apply this reading consistently.

entries.title: The size plot is never produced without a stratification file
entries.why: The behaviour is real: '~numel(...)==1' at line 108 parses as (~numel)==1, which is false for nonempty data, so lines 109-117 never run. But no option is involved: the plot is the default behaviour for nargin<6, and code that is never reached falls under wrong-result (evident intent, comment at line 107), not unusable-option. It still quarantines.

notes: Relabel the severity unusable-option as wrong-result; the quarantine stands.

entries.title: Errors when the taxon table has fewer rows than columns
entries.why: Line 42 loops to length(taxonInformation), the larger dimension; with 3 rows and 6 columns (the documented minimum of six columns) line 43 indexes row 4 and errors.

entries.title: A diet with fewer rows than columns stops with an index error
entries.why: Line 52 loops to length(dietConstraints), the larger dimension; a 1x3 or 2x3 diet (documented as three columns, any number of rows) indexes past the last row at line 54.

entries.title: Numeric bounds become NaN
entries.why: str2double of a numeric cell gives NaN (lines 54, 57, 62, 65). The header does not specify the bound type and callers pass text, so limitation is right.

entries.title: Shadow prices of the second run are dropped when the folders hold different samples
entries.why: Line 93 tests pathsRun1(i) (the i-th file of run 1) instead of pathsRun1_commonSamples(i), as line 64 does; when the i-th file is a GF file, a common non-GF sample's shadow prices from run 2 are not concatenated.

entries.title: Errors for a common germ-free sample preceded by a sample of the first run only
entries.why: The same index mismatch in reverse: the GF common sample was loaded without shadowPriceBIO (line 71), but line 93 checks the non-GF file A1, so line 95 reads the missing field.

entries.title: The skip flag 0 for VMHIDs raises an error
entries.why: exist('VMHIDs','var') at line 38 is true for any passed value, including the documented skip flag 0, so the loop brace-indexes a double at line 52; the skip branch (line 97) also misspells VMHIDS.

entries.title: similarMets is never assigned from the suggestions
entries.why: Line 179 tests ischar('similarMets'), a literal that is always true, so similarMets = suggestions never runs; with names not found and suggestSimilar 1, requesting the third output errors.

entries.title: Names of unknown IDs are dropped, so names and IDs do not line up
entries.why: intersect(...,'stable') at line 72 drops unknown IDs and duplicates, so foundMetNames is no longer aligned with the input IDs, contradicting 'names corresponding to the input IDs'.

entries.title: The numeric skip flag 0 for metNames raises an error
entries.why: Line 107 tests ~islogical(metNames), so the documented numeric flag 0 enters the names branch and line 129 brace-indexes a double; only logical false reaches the skip branch at line 183.

entries.title: Errors when the regression of a metadata variable gives a warning
entries.why: Line 255 assigns a 12-element cell to a row of the 10-variable table (line 241), so any regression that sets lastwarn (e.g. a constant metadata column) errors instead of recording NaN as the 'do not save the result' branch intends.

entries.title: The regression figures pair the values of one variable with the name of another
entries.why: significantIdx (line 285) is computed from the unsorted pValues but indexes generalTable after the sortrows at line 278, and line 328 labels sorted points with the unsorted metadataVars, so figure values and labels are mismatched.

entries.title: A text (cell array) variable of interest is not supported
entries.why: Line 162 compares metadataTable.(varOfInterest) == category, which fails for cellstr; a text variable such as Sex (the documented example) as readtable returns it is therefore a documented input that fails.

entries.title: The loadings figure of PC 1 is saved as Loadings_PC11.png
entries.why: Line 229 appends a literal "1.png" after string(PCofInterest), giving Loadings_PC11.png. Cosmetic.

entries.title: Only the first three strains are processed
entries.why: Line 26 truncates strains to strains(1:3), a debugging leftover, so only 3 strains are processed although the header says all AGORA2 strains.

entries.title: Hard-coded personal input folder
entries.why: Line 15 hard-codes a personal Windows path that line 17 immediately overrides. It has no effect on the result; cosmetic.

entries.title: Coefficients of new metabolites are written to the wrong rows
entries.why: metsToAdd comes from setdiff (sorted, line 159), but the rows are taken by matches(model2.mets, metsToAdd) (line 179), a logical mask in model 2's own order, so the coefficients of new metabolites are assigned to the wrong rows.

entries.title: Coefficients of new reactions are written to the wrong columns
entries.why: Same pattern for reactions: rxnsToAdd is sorted (line 186) while matches(model2.rxns, rxnsToAdd) (line 207) keeps model 2's order, so the new columns receive another reaction's coefficients.

entries.title: The documented default inputDir needs an explicit empty argument
entries.why: inputDir is documented with a default 'AGORA2' (line 10), but line 18 reads it unconditionally, so generatePanDatabase() fails with 'Not enough input arguments'.

entries.title: Errors for a single sample
entries.why: With one sample, filtered_abundances' (line 51) is a row vector, so bar draws a single series; line 78 then sets b(i).FaceColor for i > 1 on a placeholder and errors, although the header says 'single or multiple samples'.

entries.title: Suggestions are misaligned after a found name
entries.why: Line 63 deletes the column of a found name, but line 80 still writes the suggestions into column i of the shrunken array, so after a found name the suggestions land beside the unfound name instead of below it.

entries.title: Taxa whose name contains "pan" are counted as unmapped
entries.why: Line 118 uses erase(MARS.Taxon,'pan'), which removes every occurrence, not only the prefix ('panLactobacillus panis' becomes 'Lactobacillus is'), so such taxa are counted as unmapped. Lines 112-113 even patch two species names to work around this, which confirms the intent was to strip the prefix only.

entries.title: An unlabelled count is printed
entries.why: Line 122 is a statement without a semicolon, so 'ans = N' is printed. Cosmetic.

entries.title: The sheet of unmapped taxa is named 'Umapped'
entries.why: Line 205 writes the sheet name 'Umapped'. Cosmetic typo.

entries.title: Measured concentrations are never matched when the data has more than one row
entries.why: metConcDataBc is a cell array (lines 164, 229), so metConcDataBc{:,VMHIDCol} at line 374 (and the CSF/urine variants at 513, 603) expands into separate strcat arguments and joins all IDs into one string; ismember then matches nothing for multi-row data. The non-TEMP physiologicalConstraintsHMDBbased.m line 381 uses parentheses.

entries.title: Blood uptake constraints of organs other than the kidney are never applied
entries.why: Line 440 omits the '[bc]' suffix (the original line 447 has it), so X is empty for every organ blood exchange; the fallback lookup at line 442 sits in the if-branch and is never used, so the else branch (lines 447-457) that sets the uptake bound is never reached.

entries.title: The genus+epithet curve starts at the standard deviation of the base coverage
entries.why: Line 79 writes stdCov_readCounts(1) into meanCov_readCounts_onlyNamedTaxa(1), overwriting the mean set at line 78; stdCov_readCounts_onlyNamedTaxa(1) was clearly the target, so the genus+epithet curve starts at the SD.

entries.title: On Linux and macOS the results folder is placed at the file-system root
entries.why: The non-Windows branch at line 19 uses the backslash lookahead '.*(?=\\)', so topDir is empty for a '/' path and saveDir becomes '/Results_<folder>' at the filesystem root; mkdir fails there (or writes to the wrong place).

entries.title: A diet file path stops with an error
entries.why: Lines 50, 52, 53 and 65 use the undefined lower-case 'diet' instead of 'Diet', so the documented file-path input (a .txt file is to be skipped and returned) errors.

entries.title: Errors for germ-free and microbiome-personalised iWBMs with analyseGF
entries.why: getGfFluxFun returns a reactions-by-samples array (transposed, line 579), and meanSd (line 397) averages over dimension 1, which is over reactions. Lines 598-599 therefore assign one value per GF sample to a table with one row per reaction (line 573), which errors for the documented analyseGF = true with iWBMs and mWBMs.

entries.title: Errors when the reaction list contains a duplicate
entries.why: Duplicates are removed from reactions (line 84) and f (line 105) but not from stat, so line 111 assigns a 3-wide stat to a 2-column row. The duplicate handling at lines 81-84 shows the intent.

entries.title: Errors for more than seven phyla
entries.why: Lines 121-123 use base_colors and num_colors, which are never defined (the palette is named colors at line 108), so any input with more than 7 taxa errors.
